title: Germany news: President candidate Aigner to meet parties in Bundestag
summary: The presidential candidate put forward by the conservative bloc has said she won't meet with the far-right AfD. Meanwhile, Chancellor Merz is set to host Hungarian Prime Minister Magyar. DW has more.

image.caption: Aigner's office said she would not meet with the far-right AfD party after one its top members called her nomination a 'disgrace'Image: Odd Andersen/AFP

items: Ilse Aigner is meeting with parties in the Bundestag after being nominated by Chancellor Friedrich Merz for the presidency
Merz is hosting his Hungarian counterpart Peter Magyar in Berlin

Wadephul skeptical of Russia ahead of Abu Dhabi talks

blocks.caption: Ukraine's European partners are concerned the US will push a deal on Kyiv Image: Sebastian Christoph Gollnow/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has expressed doubt over Russia's willingness to genuinely enter into negotiation talks to end the war in Ukraine.

"Is Russia truly willing to negotiate?" he asked. Or, "is this just a negotiating charade intended to distract from the fact that Russia intends to continue a brutal war of aggression, particularly against the civilian population?"
His comments come as representatives from Ukraine and Russia began the first round of talks in nine months in Abu Dhabi. US and European representatives will also be present.
Russia "must finally give up its maximum demands," Wadephul added on the sidelines of a G7 foreign ministers meeting.
